summary: The D-227 decision-10 gate rejects only protocol ATTRIBUTES, but its own diagnostic message and every doc site say a protocol MEMBER's container type is unsupported; a protocol method parameter typed list[int] in fact lowers, compiles and runs correctly end to end
note: Reviewer found it by source reading; I reproduced it empirically. `class P(Protocol): def f(self, xs: list[int]) -> None: ...` with a conforming Impl passes `pycc check` (exit 0) and `pycc run` prints 3 (exit 0), matching CPython. So the correct repair is to narrow the wording to protocol *attributes* and pin the working method-parameter path with a test -- NOT to extend the gate, which would reject demonstrably working code. Separately, the gate's stated rationale ('structural conformance has no container case') is contradicted by that same reproduction; the real justification is that an implementing class cannot declare a matching container-typed attribute either, because ordinary class attributes are restricted to scalar slot types (verified: class attribute `xs: list[int]` is rejected as 'not a scalar slot type').

note: NOTE FOR READERS OF THIS PILE: every 'D-227' in rounds 1-3 above refers to THIS change's decision, which is now D-228. summary: The new bare-container message was not cascade-shaped, so a module whose own `class list:` failed emitted both the class's C0001 and a second diagnostic for every later `x: list` annotation, where the pre-918 tree emitted one
note: Reported by chatgpt-codex-connector as P2 on b3f8f225. Verified empirically against a `class Foo:` control (2 diagnostics vs 1) and proven a regression this PR introduces via `git show c639e682:crates/pycc_hir/src/func.rs`, which had no bare-container branch. Fixed by building the message from shared consts and teaching `cascade_name` a third parser, so a poisoned `list` suppresses the downstream annotation exactly as a poisoned `Foo` does.

summary: The bare-container advice was emitted from position-blind `annotation_to_ty`, so it recommended `list[int]` in positions where `list[int]` is itself rejected
note: Reported by chatgpt-codex-connector as P2 on b3f8f225, naming four positions (return, class attribute, dataclass field, protocol attribute). A one-file-per-position inventory measured with `target/debug/pycc check` found a fifth the review had not: the container element position, where `list[list]` advised a form T0034 rejects. Fixed by inverting the default -- `annotation_to_ty` stays generic and the five lowering positions opt in through `with_bare_container_advice` -- which covers the fifth site for free. Threading a position parameter was rejected: it makes every future call site pick a value and silently reintroduces the defect when picked wrong.

summary: A PEP 695 type parameter named after a builtin container was shadowed by the container dispatch, so `def f[list](x: list[int])` silently lowered the parameter as `Ty::List(Int)` instead of treating `list` as the type parameter
note: Reported by chatgpt-codex-connector as P2 on b3f8f225. Fixed by excluding a base name equal to the enclosing `type_param` from the container dispatch, matching the existing alias exclusion. The report was narrowed: discarding the `[int]` argument after resolving the base to `Ty::Param` is pre-existing and not introduced here -- `def f[T](x: T[int])` behaves identically on c639e682 -- so it is left alone and tracked separately.

summary: The T0053 ellipsis advice was written for `tuple` only, so `list[...]`, `set[...]` and `dict[str, ...]` all recommended `tuple[int, int]`
note: Reported by chatgpt-codex-connector as P2 on b3f8f225 and reproduced in all four families. summary: The C0001 return-position message enumerated `parameter, local-variable and type-alias` positions, omitting module-scope annotated assignments, which D-228 does lower
note: Reported by chatgpt-codex-connector as P2 on 48ed1ab6 and reproduced: `x: list[int] = [1]` at module scope exits 0. Fixed by widening the enumeration to `parameter, local- and module-variable and type-alias positions` at every site that repeats it (func.rs message and comment, pycc_diag explain.rs, the HIR unit test, the diagnostics golden file, PYTHON_STANDARDS.md and the conformance-breadth manifest), and by adding a test that lowers a container annotation in each of the five positions the advice names, so an enumeration that drifts from the compiler's behaviour fails.

summary: A module-level function, value or import binding named after a container builtin does not suppress the container dispatch, so `def list(...)` followed by `x: list[int]` still lowers as `Ty::List(Int)`
note: Reported by chatgpt-codex-connector as P2 on 48ed1ab6 and reproduced: the two-definition program exits 0 with no diagnostic. Filed as issue #932 (v0.4) rather than fixed here. The gate already covers the three shadow sources `annotation_to_ty` can see (known classes, the enclosing type parameter, aliases); covering module bindings needs a binding set threaded through ~19 call sites plus a scoping decision the report does not settle -- whether a value binding (`list = 5`), an import binding, or a binding that appears after the annotation participates. The consequence is bounded: pycc accepts a program CPython rejects at run time, not a miscompilation. It is not a regression of previously-correct behaviour either -- before Part 1 every parameterized container annotation was rejected, so no version distinguished this case.
